hints: Think about how the airway wall changes as tubes get narrower from trachea to bronchi to tiny bronchioles, especially the stiff support tissue.
Remember which tissues must line every airway for protection and which muscle controls airflow diameter, versus cartilage which is only needed to hold large airways open.
walkthrough:
**Picture the airways getting smaller**

Think of air travelling down: trachea to bronchi to bronchioles. The walls change as the tubes get narrower.

Large tubes need stiff support to stay open. Tiny tubes need flexible control of diameter instead.

**Test each structure for both locations**

1 cartilage: present as C-shaped rings in the trachea, but it gets smaller and disappears. No cartilage in bronchioles at all.

2 smooth muscle: present in the trachea and in all bronchioles, where it contracts to narrow the airway.

3 epithelial cells: present everywhere, as the lining of the whole airway system.

**Choose the shared structures**

Only 2 and 3 are found in both the trachea and in all bronchioles. Cartilage (1) is missing from bronchioles.

That gives 2 and 3 only.

options.A: Includes cartilage, but cartilage is absent from bronchioles so 1, 2 and 3 cannot all be shared.
options.B: Cartilage alone is wrong because it is in the trachea but not in bronchioles.
options.C: Correct, both smooth muscle and epithelial cells line the trachea and continue into all bronchioles.
options.D: Smooth muscle alone is incomplete because epithelial cells are also present in both locations.
